item.title: Michael Nielsen takes down his deep learning textbook over frontier AI safety concerns
item.description: Nielsen’s decision highlights a sharp critique: technical AI alignment isn't solving existential risk, but rather acting as commercial polish that accelerates a race our social institutions cannot handle.

item.title: Neuroimaging reveals covert consciousness in comatose ICU patients, challenging traditional end-of-life protocols
item.description: The discovery that a significant fraction of comatose patients retain covert consciousness forces us to reconsider both diagnostic protocols in the ICU and how we evaluate prognosis during end-of-life decisions.

item.title: Systemic Screening Gaps Leave Perinatal Eating Disorders Largely Undiagnosed and Untreated
item.description: Because ACOG lacks formal clinical guidelines for perinatal eating disorders, state health policies completely omit screening for conditions that affect up to nine percent of new mothers.

item.title: Sodium-ion batteries emerge as cheap, supply-secure alternatives for grid energy storage
item.description: Sodium-ion won't replace lithium in EVs tomorrow, but for stationary grid storage and AI data centers, its thermal stability and supply chain security make it the inevitable backstop.

item.title: A Swedish clinic offers formal reassessment and removal of ADHD and autism diagnoses
item.description: The Swedish clinic highlights how rigid career bans and shifting diagnostic criteria are forcing a debate on whether ADHD and autism are truly lifelong.

item.title: Why non-frontier tech leaders must independently reproduce AI lab results under real-world constraints
item.description: The real test of AI isn't what frontier labs claim in their marketing, but whether non-lab companies can independently reproduce those results within real budget and IT constraints.

item.title: Kyiv endures winter infrastructure strikes while rejecting transactional US peace proposals
item.description: The fundamental flaw in Western peace proposals is treating the war like a corporate transaction, ignoring that Putin sees victory as personal survival while Ukrainians view it as an existential matter of national identity.

item.title: Framing the AI Apocalypse Through Tangible Defenses Against Privacy and Truth Decay
item.description: The most plausible AI threat isn't physical destruction, but a subtle collapse of shared reality and human expertise that requires intentional, low-tech friction to counter.

item.title: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham Reopens the Brexit Debate to Rebuild European Ties
item.description: Burnham is cleverly flipping the script on Brexit by framing E.U. rapprochement not as an ideological retreat, but as a practical fix for stunted economic growth and supply chain friction.

item.title: European Exoneration Database Reveals Systemic Causes of Wrongful Convictions and Lost Years
item.description: The data from Europe's new exoneration registry shows wrongful convictions aren't rare anomalies, but predictable systemic failures driven by false confessions and flawed forensics that leave real offenders free.

item.title: Kahlil Gibran’s 1918 Parable Explores Fragmented Identity and the Power of Stillness
item.description: Gibran’s parable is a sharp reminder that the busy, driven facets of identity only settle when anchored by an observant, quiet center.

item.title: Graph Theorists Prove Exact Four-Structure Limit for Perfect Computer Network Resilience
item.description: It turns out adding more connections to a network can actually make perfect resilience impossible, because dense graphs are far more likely to contain one of the four structural patterns that cause infinite loops.
